translationRepairs: Saturn appears egg-shaped; older observers spoke of "ears," but telescopes show a narrow ring edge-on near the equatorial stars and a broad ring when seen obliquely.
Saturn appears egg-shaped; older observers spoke of "ears," but new measures find the disk very narrow near the equator and very wide far from the equator.

s0007 says 今測近於赤道星面相逼甚窄，於遠赤道所宕甚寬: 星面 is Saturn's disk face near the equator, not equatorial stars, and 今測 is new measures, not telescopes or an edge-on/oblique ring gloss. The proposed idiomatic restores that sense without inventing ring geometry.
Saturn's body is egg-shaped; old measures said two ears at its sides; new measures find the disk near the equatorial stars very narrow and the disk far from the equator very wide.
Saturn's body is egg-shaped; old measures said two ears at its sides; new measures find the disk near the equator very narrow and far from the equator very wide.
The same clause 近於赤道星面 is 赤道 + 星面 (disk near the equator), not 赤道星. The prior literal's 'equatorial stars' is a false parse; the proposed literal matches the Chinese.
Cold Dew—dusk: Northern Dipper, 53′ west of the meridian.
Cold Dew—dusk: Ox, 53′ west of the meridian.
s0161 has 寒露昏牽牛中; 牽牛 is the Ox lodge. Northern Dipper would be 北斗, absent here; 'Ox' is the correct lodge name.
Cold Dew—dusk: Northern Dipper on the meridian, 53′ west of center.
Cold Dew—dusk: Ox on the meridian, 53′ west of center.
Literal English likewise renders 牽牛 as Northern Dipper; the Chinese names the Ox lodge culminating at Cold Dew dusk. 'Ox on the meridian' is accurate.
Clear Bright—dusk: Seven Culminating Stars, 5° 14′ east of the meridian.
Clear Bright—dusk: Seven Stars, 5° 14′ east of the meridian.

Neighboring dusk lines use lodge + 中 (東井中, and dawn 房中 / 帝座中). 七中星 is the same formula with 中 and 星 transposed for the lodge 七星, not a distinct 'Seven Culminating Stars' asterism; 'Seven Stars' matches that reading.
Clear Bright—dusk: Seven Culminating Stars on the meridian, 5° 14′ east of center.
Clear Bright—dusk: Seven Stars on the meridian, 5° 14′ east of center.
The literal should name the lodge 七星 under the same dusk-culmination pattern, not treat 七中星 as a separate asterism title. 'Seven Stars on the meridian' is the correct literal.

units.zh: 日月五星自古言天之精者，知日月五星為渾象而已。
units.en: Since antiquity, heaven's "essence" was understood as no more than the sun, moon, and five planets modeled on the armillary sphere.
units.literal: Sun, moon, and five planets—from antiquity those who spoke of heaven's essence knew them only as the armillary-sphere image.

units.zh: 近代西人制大遠鏡，測得諸曜形體及附近小星暈氣各種，古今不同，就其著者錄焉。
units.en: Recently Westerners built great telescopes and mapped planetary bodies, companion stars, halos, and vapors as their authors recorded—unlike anything known in antiquity.
units.literal: In recent times Westerners made great telescopes and measured the luminaries' bodies and nearby small stars, halos, vapors, and the like—each age differing; here what their authors recorded.

units.zh: 日之面有小黑形，常運行二十八日滿一周。
units.en: Sunspots appear on the solar disk and complete one revolution in twenty-eight days.
units.literal: On the sun's face are small black shapes, constantly moving to complete one circuit in twenty-eight days.

units.zh: 月之面以日光正照顯明景，偏照顯黑景。
units.en: Full sunlight on the moon yields bright terrain; grazing light yields shadowed terrain.
units.literal: The moon's face shows bright scenery under direct sunlight and dark scenery under oblique light.

units.zh: 其面有凹凸，故雖全明之中，亦有淡黑雜景。
units.en: Lunar relief leaves faint dark patches even at full phase.
units.literal: Its surface has highs and lows, so even at full brightness faint dark patches mingle.

units.zh: 土星之體，彷彿卵形，舊測謂旁有兩耳，今測近於赤道星面相逼甚窄，於遠赤道所宕甚寬。
units.en: Saturn appears egg-shaped; older observers spoke of "ears," but new measures find the disk very narrow near the equator and very wide far from the equator.
units.literal: Saturn's body is egg-shaped; old measures said two ears at its sides; new measures find the disk near the equator very narrow and far from the equator very wide.

units.zh: 旁有排定小星五點，最近第一星，約行二日弱；
units.en: Five attendant stars lie beside it; the innermost completes a circuit in just over two days;
units.literal: At its side are five fixed small stars; the nearest first star travels in a little over two days;

units.zh: 第二星行三日弱；
units.en: the second in just over three;
units.literal: the second star in a little over three days;

units.zh: 第三星行四日半強；
units.en: the third in about four and a half days;
units.literal: the third in four and a half days plus;

units.zh: 第四星略大，行十六日；
units.en: the fourth, somewhat larger, in sixteen days;
units.literal: the fourth, slightly larger, in sixteen days;

units.zh: 第五星行八十日。
units.en: the fifth in eighty days.
units.literal: the fifth in eighty days.

units.zh: 俱旋行土星一周。
units.en: All orbit Saturn once per revolution.
units.literal: All revolve once around Saturn.

units.zh: 木星之面，常有平行暗景，外有小星四點。
units.en: Jupiter shows parallel dark belts with four small stars outside.
units.literal: Jupiter's face often shows parallel dark bands; outside are four small stars.

units.zh: 第一星行一日七十三刻；
units.en: The innermost moon: one day and seventy-three quarters;
units.literal: The first star travels one day and seventy-three quarters;

units.zh: 第二星行三日五十三刻；
units.en: the second: three days and fifty-three quarters;
units.literal: the second three days and fifty-three quarters;

units.zh: 第三星略大，行七日十六刻；
units.en: the third, larger: seven days and sixteen quarters;
units.literal: the third, slightly larger, seven days and sixteen quarters;

units.zh: 第四星行十六日七十二刻。
units.en: the fourth: sixteen days and seventy-two quarters.
units.literal: the fourth sixteen days and seventy-two quarters.

units.zh: 俱旋行木星一周。
units.en: All orbit Jupiter once per revolution.
units.literal: All revolve once around Jupiter.

units.zh: 火星之面，內有無定黑景。
units.en: Mars shows shifting dark markings on its disk.
units.literal: Mars's face has irregular dark patches within.

units.zh: 金、水星俱借日為光，合朔弦望如月。
units.en: Venus and Mercury shine by reflected sunlight and show lunar-like phases from conjunction through full.
units.literal: Venus and Mercury both borrow the sun's light; at conjunction, first quarter, full, and last quarter they are like the moon.

units.zh: 恆星曆象考成云：「恆星之名，見於春秋，而四仲中星及斗、牽牛、織女、參、昴、箕、畢、大火、農祥、龍尾、鳥帑、元駟、元黿之屬，散見於尚書、易、詩、左傳、國語。
units.en: The Fixed Stars section of the Calendar Compilation notes: "Star names appear in the Spring and Autumn Annals; midpoint stars of the four seasons and groups such as the Dipper, Ox, Weaver, Shen, Mao, Ji, Bi, Great Fire, Nongxiang, Dragon Tail, Bird Banner, Yuanji, and Yuanyuan recur across the Classics.
units.literal: The Fixed Stars Calendar and Phenomena Compilation says: "Names of fixed stars appear in the Spring and Autumn Annals; the four seasonal midpoint stars and Dipper, Ox, Weaver, Shen, Mao, Ji, Bi, Great Fire, Nongxiang, Dragon Tail, Bird Banner, Yuanji, Yuanyuan and the like are scattered through the Documents, Changes, Odes, Zuo Commentary, and Discourses of the States.

units.zh: 至周禮春官馮相氏掌二十八星之位，而禮記月令、大戴禮夏小正稍具諸星見伏之節。
units.en: The Zhou Ritual's astronomer tracked the twenty-eight mansions; the Monthly Ordinances and Great Dai's Summer Annals further fixed when stars rose and set.
units.literal: By the Zhou Ritual's Director of Astronomy who kept the positions of the twenty-eight stars, and the Monthly Ordinances of the Book of Rites and the Great Dai's Lesser Annals of Summer, the seasons of stars' appearance and hiding were somewhat complete.

units.zh: 蓋古者敬天勤民，因時出政，皆以星為紀。
units.en: Ancient rulers revered heaven, served the people, and timed policy by the stars.
units.literal: In antiquity men revered heaven and toiled for the people; issuing government by season—all took stars as their record.

units.zh: 秦炬之後，羲和舊術，無復可稽，其傳者惟史記天官書，而所載簡略。
units.en: After the Qin bibliocaust the Xihe tradition was lost; only Sima Qian's Heavenly Offices survives, and briefly.
units.literal: After the Qin burning, the old arts of Xihe could no longer be traced; what survived was only the Grand Historian's Treatise on the Heavenly Offices, and what it records is brief.

units.zh: 後漢張衡云：『中外之官，常明者百有二十四，可名者三百二十，為星二千五百』，而其書不傳。
units.en: Zhang Heng of Later Han wrote that 'Of inner and outer offices, those always bright are 124; nameable ones 320; stars 2,500'—yet his treatise is lost.
units.literal: Later Han Zhang Heng said: 'Of inner and outer offices, those always bright are one hundred twenty-four; nameable ones three hundred twenty; stars two thousand five hundred'—yet his book does not survive.

units.zh: 至三國時，太史令陳卓始列巫咸、甘、石三家所著星圖，總二百八十三官，一千四百六十四星。
units.en: In the Three Kingdoms, Chen Zhuo compiled star maps by Wu Xian, Gan, and Shi: 283 offices and 1,464 stars.
units.literal: By the Three Kingdoms, Grand Clerk Chen Zhuo first arrayed the star charts of Wu Xian, Gan, and Shi, totaling two hundred eighty-three offices and one thousand four hundred sixty-four stars.

units.zh: 隋丹元子作步天歌，敘三垣二十八宿，共一千四百六十七星，為觀象之津梁，然尚未有各星經緯度數。
units.en: Dan Yuanzi's Steps to Heaven Song (Sui) listed the Three Enclosures and Twenty-eight Mansions—1,467 stars—as a sky-watcher's guide, but gave no per-star coordinates.
units.literal: Sui's Dan Yuanzi made the Steps to Heaven Song, treating the Three Enclosures and Twenty-eight Mansions—one thousand four hundred sixty-seven stars in all—as a bridge for observing the sky, yet there were still no each-star ecliptic and equatorial degrees.

units.zh: 自唐、宋而後，諸家以儀象考測，始有各星入宿去極度分，視古加密。
units.en: From Tang and Song, instrument surveys yielded lodge longitudes and polar distances for individual stars—far finer than older catalogs.
units.literal: From Tang and Song onward, schools measured with armillary instruments and began to have each star's lodge entry and polar distance in degrees and minutes—denser than antiquity.

units.zh: 「新法算書恆星圖表，共星一千二百六十六，分為六等：第一等星一十七，第二等星五十七，第三等星一百八十五，第四等星三百八十九，第五等星三百二十三，第六等星二百九十五，外無名不入等者四百五十九。
units.en: The New Methods Calculation Book catalogs 1,266 stars in six magnitudes: 17 of the first, 57 of the second, 185 of the third, 389 of the fourth, 323 of the fifth, 295 of the sixth, plus 459 ungraded and unnamed.
units.literal: The New Methods Calculation Book's fixed-star tables list one thousand two hundred sixty-six stars in six grades: first magnitude seventeen, second fifty-seven, third one hundred eighty-five, fourth three hundred eighty-nine, fifth three hundred twenty-three, sixth two hundred ninety-five, and four hundred fifty-nine unnamed below grade.

units.zh: 康熙壬子年欽天監新修儀象志，恆星亦分六等，而其數微異。
units.en: The Kangxi Directorate's 1672 Observational Instruments Treatise also ranks stars in six grades, with slightly different totals.
units.literal: In Kangxi renzi the Directorate revised the Observational Instruments Treatise; fixed stars were also divided into six grades, but the counts differ slightly.

units.zh: 第一等星一十六，第二等星六十八，第三等星二百零八，第四等星五百一十二，第五等星三百四十二，第六等星七百三十二，共計一千八百七十八。
units.en: Sixteen of the first magnitude, sixty-eight of the second, 208 of the third, 512 of the fourth, 342 of the fifth, 732 of the sixth—1,878 in all.
units.literal: First magnitude sixteen, second sixty-eight, third two hundred eight, fourth five hundred twelve, fifth three hundred forty-two, sixth seven hundred thirty-two—total one thousand eight hundred seventy-eight.

units.zh: 蓋觀星者以目之所能辨，因其相近，聯綴成象而命之名。
units.en: Observers group stars the eye can resolve into figures and name them.
units.literal: Observers name stars by what the eye can distinguish, linking nearby ones into a figure and giving it a name.

units.zh: 其微茫昏暗者，多不可考。
units.en: Faint stars mostly defy reliable identification.
units.literal: The dim and faint mostly cannot be verified.

units.zh: 故各家星官之數，多少不能畫一。
units.en: So star-office totals differ from school to school.
units.literal: Hence the counts of star offices in each school cannot be made uniform.

units.zh: 然列宿及諸大星，則古今中西如一轍也。」
units.en: Major mansions and bright stars nonetheless agree across antiquity, China, and the West."
units.literal: Yet the mansions and the great stars are the same in antiquity, China, and the West."

units.zh: 又云：「恆星行即古歲差也，古法俱謂恆星不動，而黃道西移；
units.en: It adds: "Apparent fixed-star motion is precession. Classical theory held stars fixed while the ecliptic drifted westward;
units.literal: It also says: "Fixed-star motion is the ancient precession; old methods all held fixed stars unmoving while the ecliptic shifted west;

units.zh: 今謂黃道不動，而恆星東行。
units.en: modern theory holds the ecliptic fixed and stars drifting eastward.
units.literal: now it is held the ecliptic is unmoving while fixed stars move east.

units.zh: 蓋使恆星不動而黃道西移，則恆星之黃道經緯度宜每歲不同，而赤道經緯度宜終古不變。
units.en: If stars were fixed and only the ecliptic moved west, stellar ecliptic coordinates would change yearly but equatorial ones would not.
units.literal: If fixed stars were unmoving and the ecliptic shifted west, fixed stars' ecliptic longitude and latitude should differ each year while equatorial longitude and latitude should never change.

units.zh: 今測恆星之黃道經度，每歲東行，而緯度不變。
units.en: Measurement shows ecliptic longitude increasing eastward yearly with latitude constant.
units.literal: Now measuring fixed stars' ecliptic longitude, each year they move east while latitude is unchanged.

units.zh: 至於赤道經度，則逐歲不同，而緯度尤甚。
units.en: Equatorial longitude changes annually; latitude changes even more.
units.literal: As for equatorial longitude, it differs year by year, and latitude even more so.

units.zh: 自星紀至鶉首六宮之星，在赤道南者，緯度古多而今漸少，在赤道北者反是。
units.en: From Xingji through Zuishou, stars south of the equator show higher ancient latitudes that now decrease; northern stars show the opposite.
units.literal: Among stars of the six palaces from Xingji to Zuishou, those south of the equator have latitude greater in antiquity and gradually less now; those north of the equator the reverse.

units.zh: 自鶉首至星紀六宮之星，在赤道南者，緯度古少而今漸多，在赤道北者反是。
units.en: From Zuishou back to Xingji, southern stars show lower ancient latitudes that now increase; northern stars reverse again.
units.literal: Among stars of the six palaces from Zuishou to Xingji, those south of the equator have latitude less in antiquity and gradually more now; those north of the equator the reverse.

units.zh: 凡距赤道二十三度半以內之星，在赤道北者，可以過赤道南，在赤道南者，亦可以過赤道北，則恆星循黃道東行，而非黃道之西移明矣。
units.en: Stars within 23.5° of the equator can cross it north or south—proof that stars move east along the ecliptic rather than the ecliptic sliding west.
units.literal: For all stars within twenty-three and a half degrees of the equator, those north of the equator may cross to the south, and those south may cross north—then fixed stars move east along the ecliptic, and the ecliptic's westward shift is clear.

units.zh: 新法算書載西人第谷以前，或云恆星百年而東行一度，或云七十餘年而東行一度，或云六十餘年而東行一度，隨時修改，訖無定數，與古人屢改歲差相同。
units.en: Before Tycho, Westerners guessed precession at one degree per century, per seventy-odd years, or per sixty-odd—each revision unsettled, mirroring China's shifting precession rates.
units.literal: The New Methods Calculation Book records that before the Westerner Tycho some said fixed stars move east one degree in a hundred years, some in seventy-odd, some in sixty-odd—revised with the times, never settled—like the ancients' repeated changes to precession.

units.zh: 迨至第谷，方定恆星每歲東行五十一秒，約七十年有餘而行一度，而元郭守敬所定歲差之數亦為近之。
units.en: Tycho fixed annual eastward motion at 51 seconds—about one degree in seventy years—close to Guo Shoujing's Yuan rate.
units.literal: Only at Tycho was it fixed that fixed stars move east fifty-one seconds each year—about seventy-odd years for one degree—and the Yuan's Guo Shoujing's precession number is also close.

units.zh: 至今一百四十餘年，驗之於天，雖無差忒，但星行微渺，必歷多年，其差乃見。
units.en: Observations over 140 years show no error yet, though such minute drift needs centuries to expose.
units.literal: To the present, one hundred forty-odd years verified in the sky show no error, yet star motion is minute and only after many years does the discrepancy appear.

units.zh: 然則第谷所定之數，亦未可泥為定率，惟隨時測驗，依天行以推其數可也。」
units.en: Tycho's rate should not be treated as eternal; periodic measurement must track heaven's actual motion."
units.literal: Then Tycho's fixed number also cannot be taken as an immutable rate; only by measuring in season and inferring the number from heaven's motion will do."

units.en: (closing quotation mark in the source.)
units.literal: (closing quotation mark in the source.)

units.zh: 儀象考成云：「康熙十三年，監臣南懷仁修儀象志，星名與古同者，總二百五十九座，一千一百二十九星，比步天歌少二十四座，三百三十五星。
units.en: The Compendium records: "In 1674 Verbiest revised the star catalog to 259 offices and 1,129 named stars matching antiquity—24 offices and 335 stars fewer than the Steps to Heaven Song.
units.literal: The Compendium of Observational Instruments says: "In Kangxi 13, supervising official Ferdinand Verbiest revised the Observational Instruments Treatise; star names matching antiquity totaled two hundred fifty-nine offices and one thousand one hundred twenty-nine stars—twenty-four offices and three hundred thirty-five stars fewer than the Steps to Heaven Song.

units.zh: 又於有名常數之外，增五百九十七星。
units.en: Another 597 stars were added beyond the classical named set.
units.literal: Beyond named constants, five hundred ninety-seven stars were added.

units.zh: 又多近南極星二十三座，一百五十星。
units.en: Twenty-three south polar offices with 150 stars were added.
units.literal: Also twenty-three offices and one hundred fifty stars near the south pole.

units.zh: 近年以來，累加測驗，星官度數，儀象志尚多未合。
units.en: Recent remeasurements show many coordinates still diverging from Verbiest's treatise.
units.literal: In recent years repeated measurement and verification show many star-office degrees still not matching the Observational Instruments Treatise.

units.zh: 又星之次第多不序順，亦宜釐正。
units.en: Star sequences, too, were often out of order and needed correction.
units.literal: Also the ordering of stars is often not sequential and should be rectified.

units.zh: 於是逐星測量，推其度數，觀其形象，序其次第，著之於圖。
units.en: Officials then measured each star, derived coordinates, noted figures, fixed sequence, and charted the sky anew.
units.literal: Thereupon each star was measured, its degrees inferred, its figure observed, its sequence ordered, and set down in charts.

units.zh: 計三垣二十八宿，星名與古同者，總二百七十七座，一千三百一十九星，比儀象志多十八座，一百九十星，與步天歌為近。
units.en: The revised Three Enclosures and Twenty-eight Mansions list 277 offices and 1,319 classical stars—18 offices and 190 stars more than Verbiest, nearer the Steps to Heaven Song.
units.literal: Counting the Three Enclosures and Twenty-eight Mansions, star names matching antiquity totaled two hundred seventy-seven offices and one thousand three hundred nineteen stars—eighteen offices and one hundred ninety stars more than the Observational Instruments Treatise, close to the Steps to Heaven Song.

units.zh: 其尤與古合者，二十八宿次舍，自古皆觜宿在前，參宿在後，其以何星作距，古無明文。
units.en: Classical lodge order always placed Zi (Mouth) before Shen (Three Stars); which star was the determining star remained undocumented.
units.literal: What especially matched antiquity: for the twenty-eight mansions' successive lodges, from antiquity Mouth (Zi) was always before Shen; which star served as determining star antiquity left unstated.

units.zh: 唐書云：『古以參右肩為距』，失之太遠。
units.en: The Tang History claims the ancient determining star for Shen was its right shoulder—far too remote.
units.literal: The Tang History says: 'In antiquity Shen's right shoulder was taken as determining star'—too far off.

units.zh: 文獻通考載宋兩朝天文志云：『觜三星，距西南星；
units.en: The Wenxian Tongkao quotes Song astronomical treatises: "For Zi's three stars, the determining star is the southwestern one;
units.literal: The Wenxian Tongkao cites the Song dynasties' Astronomical Treatises: 'Mouth—three stars, determining star the southwest star;

units.zh: 參十星，距中星西一星。』
units.en: for Shen's ten stars, the star one step west of the center."
units.literal: Shen—ten stars, determining star the one west of the center star.'

units.zh: 西法，觜宿距中上星，參宿亦距中西一星。
units.en: Western method makes Zi's determining star the central upper star and Shen's the star west of center.
units.literal: Western method: Zi lodge's determining star is the central upper star; Shen also takes the one west of center.

units.zh: 今按觜宿中上星在西南星前僅六分餘，而西南星小，中上星大，則以中上星作距可也。
units.en: Zi's central upper star precedes the southwestern by only six minutes and is brighter—so it rightly serves as determining star.
units.literal: Now examining Zi's central upper star: it lies only six-odd minutes before the southwest star, yet the southwest star is small and the central upper large—so the central upper may serve as determining star.

units.zh: 若參宿以中西一星作距星，則觜宿之黃道度已在參宿後一度餘，即赤道度亦在參宿後三十一分餘。
units.en: If Shen's determining star is west of center, Zi's ecliptic longitude falls over a degree past Shen—thirty-one minutes past in equatorial longitude.
units.literal: If Shen takes the west-of-center star as determining star, then Zi's ecliptic degree already lies more than one degree behind Shen—and equatorial degree more than thirty-one minutes behind Shen.

units.zh: 今依次順序，以參宿中三星之東一星作距星，則觜宿黃道度恆在參前一度弱，與觜前參後之序合。
units.en: Taking the eastern of Shen's central trio as determining star keeps Zi about one degree ahead of Shen, preserving classical Zi-before-Shen order.
units.literal: Now following sequence, taking the eastern of Shen's three center stars as determining star, Zi's ecliptic degree always stands a little over one degree before Shen—matching the order of Zi before Shen.

units.zh: 其餘諸座之星，皆以次順序，無凌躐顛倒之弊。
units.en: Other mansions were sequenced likewise, without leap or reversal.
units.literal: The remaining offices' stars all follow in sequence without leap or inversion.

units.zh: 又於有名常數之外，增一千六百一十四星。
units.en: Another 1,614 supplemental stars were catalogued.
units.literal: Beyond named constants, one thousand six hundred fourteen stars were added.

units.zh: 近某座者即名某座增星，依次分註方位，以備稽考。
units.en: Stars near a mansion were labeled as its supplemental stars with positional notes for lookup.
units.literal: Those near a given office were named supplemental stars of that office, with direction noted in sequence for reference.

units.zh: 其近南極星二十三座，一百五十星，中國所不見，仍依西測之舊。
units.en: Twenty-three south polar offices (150 stars) unseen in China retain Western survey coordinates.
units.literal: The twenty-three south polar offices and one hundred fifty stars invisible in China still follow the old Western survey.

units.zh: 共計恆星三百座，三千八十三星。」
units.en: In all: 300 offices and 3,083 stars."
units.literal: Total: three hundred star offices, three thousand eighty-three stars."

units.en: (closing quotation mark in the source.)
units.literal: (closing quotation mark in the source.)

units.zh: 黃赤道十二次值宿古者分十二次即節氣，故冬至為丑中，春分為戌中，夏至為未中，秋分為辰中。
units.en: The twelve ecliptic stations originally aligned with solar terms: winter solstice at mid-Chou, spring equinox at mid-Xu, summer solstice at mid-Wei, autumn equinox at mid-Chen.
units.literal: Yellow and red-path twelve stations and lodge assignments: antiquity divided twelve stations as solar terms, so winter solstice was at Chou's center, spring equinox at Xu's center, summer solstice at Wei's center, autumn equinox at Chen's center.

units.zh: 後人則以中氣，而冬至在星紀之初。
units.en: Later astronomers used mid-climate points, placing winter solstice at the beginning of Xingji.
units.literal: Later men used mid-climate qi, so winter solstice fell at the start of Xingji.

units.zh: 古不知列宿循黃道東行，且不見有歲差，即以所在星象名其次，故奎、婁為降婁，房、心、尾為大火，後人悉仍其名，而星象之更則不論。
units.en: Unaware of precession, ancients named stations for then-current constellations—so Kui-Lou became Jianglou and Fang-Heart-Tail Great Fire—names later generations kept though the stars moved on.
units.literal: Antiquity did not know mansions drift east along the ecliptic and did not see precession; they named each station from the starry figure then present—hence Kui and Lou are Jianglou, Fang, Heart, and Tail are Great Fire; later men kept the names while the figures shifted.

units.zh: 積數千年，將所謂蒼龍、玄武、白虎、硃雀之四象且易其方，然則十二次之名，存古意爾。
units.en: Given millennial drift, even the Four Symbols would swap quadrants; the twelve station names preserve only ancient meaning.
units.literal: Over thousands of years the Azure Dragon, Black Tortoise, White Tiger, and Vermilion Bird would even exchange quarters; the twelve stations' names preserve ancient intent only.

units.zh: 今以康熙甲子年推定十二次初度所值宿，及乾隆甲子年改定十二次初度所值宿，並紀於左。

units.literal: Now the lodges at each twelve-station initial degree are fixed for Kangxi jiazi and revised for Qianlong jiazi, all recorded at left.

units.en: Dusk-and-dawn meridian stars begin in the Book of Yu with the four seasons' dusk culminations; the Monthly Ordinances give dusk and dawn month by month.
units.literal: Dusk-and-dawn meridian stars: the Book of Yu records the four seasons' dusk-culminating stars, while the Monthly Ordinances list dusk and dawn for every month.

units.zh: 然虞書仲冬星昴，月令則昏中東壁，相去約二千年，中星相差四宿。
units.en: The Book of Yu has Hairy Head at mid-winter culmination; the Monthly Ordinances have Eastern Wall at dusk—two millennia apart, four lodges between them.
units.literal: Yet the Book of Yu places Hairy Head at mid-winter culmination, while the Monthly Ordinances place Eastern Wall at dusk—some two thousand years apart, with the meridian stars differing by four lodges.

units.zh: 雖由歲差之故，而古法疏略無度分，固難深論也。
units.en: Precession explains the drift, but old methods lack fine degrees and minutes—there is little ground for a close dispute.
units.literal: Though precession accounts for this, the ancient methods are coarse and lack degree-and-minute precision, so one cannot press the argument far.

units.zh: 今以康熙壬子年所定恆星經緯度，推得雍正元年癸卯各節氣昏旦中星列於志。
units.en: Using Kangxi renzi fixed-star coordinates, we derive Yongzheng guimao dusk-and-dawn meridian stars for each solar term and list them here.
units.literal: Here, from the fixed stars' longitude and latitude set in the Kangxi renzi year, are derived the dusk-and-dawn meridian stars for each solar term in the Yongzheng inaugural year guimao, recorded in this treatise.

units.zh: 若求乾隆九年甲子以後各節氣昏旦中星，則當按乾隆甲子年改定恆星經緯度備推焉。
units.en: For solar terms after Qianlong 9 jiazi, use the Qianlong jiazi fixed-star revision as the basis for calculation.
units.literal: To obtain dusk-and-dawn meridian stars for solar terms after Qianlong 9 jiazi, one should compute from the fixed-star coordinates revised in the Qianlong jiazi year.

units.en: Awakening of Insects—dusk: Eastern Well, 3° 6′ west of the meridian.
units.literal: Awakening of Insects—dusk: Eastern Well on the meridian, 3° 6′ west of center.

units.en: Dawn: Room, 2° 4′ west of the meridian.
units.literal: Dawn: Room on the meridian, 2° 4′ west of center.

units.zh: 清明昏七中星偏東五度十四分。
units.en: Clear Bright—dusk: Seven Stars, 5° 14′ east of the meridian.
units.literal: Clear Bright—dusk: Seven Stars on the meridian, 5° 14′ east of center.

units.zh: 旦帝座中偏東一度五十九分。
units.en: Dawn: Emperor's Seat, 1° 59′ east of the meridian.
units.literal: Dawn: Emperor's Seat on the meridian, 1° 59′ east of center.
